clue.text: Question trainee got wrong about arithmetic maybe

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, surrounding, the single letter from arithmetic
letters that have gone wrong are out of order, so trainee and got are rearranged

parts.note: arithmetic is one of the three Rs of basic schooling, so it stands for R

explanation.surface: A trainee has bungled a sum, and someone asks about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got wrong' reads as the trainee's mistake, but 'wrong' is the anagram signal; arithmetic is one of the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic), so 'about' wraps the jumble round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone closely is the verb sense of the answer, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Retreats as negative vote's accepting sanction

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a negative vote is a no; plural noes gives NOS
to sanction is to approve, to OK

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws because a vote went against them despite approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreats as quiet secluded corners: a nook is a sheltered hideaway, so these are plural synonyms.

clue.text: Cheer and cheer, concealing envy, oddly

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something inside, so the picked letters go within

parts.note: to cheer someone is to elate them

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the word envy

explanation.surface: Raising spirits twice over while hiding one's jealousy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st and 3rd letters of envy, E and V, which 'concealing' puts inside ELATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate someone's mood is to lift or cheer them, a synonym for raising spirits.

clue.text: Leave government split by factions conclusively

indicators.note: split by means the word is broken open and the other letter is put in it

parts.note: to reign is to rule, the period of a monarch's government

indicators.note: conclusively means the final letter of the word factions

explanation.surface: Factions have torn a government apart, so it's time to step down.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to quit a job, a synonym for leaving a post.

clue.text: Grand at first, cad embracing one's more seedy

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letter of the word Grand
embracing means holding something inside, so the cad word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a cad is a rotter, an old-fashioned word for a scoundrel
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A grand cad hugs someone shabbier than himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Grotty is British slang for shabby or unpleasant, so its comparative matches seedier.

clue.text: Tiresome editor promises to pay after time

indicators.note: after places the editor and promises to pay behind the time letter

parts.note: an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt; plural IOUS

explanation.surface: A dull editor keeps issuing IOUs over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome and boring are close synonyms: something tedious wearies you.

clue.text: Uncaring behind bars holding criminal on charge

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the criminal goes within the jail word

parts.note: a prisoner behind bars is inside, slang for in jail
a con is a convict, a criminal
a charge is a price or rate

explanation.surface: A heartless prisoner is jailed holding a criminal on a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply joins the charge word after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsiderate means thoughtless of others, a synonym for uncaring.

clue.text: Beam with nice well-disposed feeling

indicators.note: read as disposed well, the letters of beam and nice are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Beaming at someone nice gives a friendly glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-disposed' looks like a description of a friendly mood but read as 'disposed well' it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambience is the mood or atmosphere of a place, the feeling it gives off.

clue.text: I contort spine awkwardly for self-examination

indicators.note: awkwardly means the letters are put in an ungainly new order

explanation.surface: Someone twists their back uncomfortably while thinking about themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Introspection is looking inward at one's own thoughts, so it is a synonym for self-examination.

clue.text: Nothing in beak but rope

indicators.note: in means the nothing letter goes inside the beak word

parts.note: beak is slang for the nose
nothing is zero, shown by the letter O

explanation.surface: A bird's bill holds only a rope, nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: Beak is also British slang for a magistrate, adding to the courtroom flavour of rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot, as on a hangman's rope.

clue.text: Second's words managed to carry fighter

indicators.note: the phrase second's words managed is said to carry the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A boxer's second managed to say something to support their fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: The words look like a charade of S + WORDS + MAN, but the letters simply run on inside 'Second's words managed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordsman is one who fights with a blade, so a type of fighter.

clue.text: Some person's laughter is offensive

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people's laughter can be insulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is offensive' reads as a verb phrase: the noun sense is an attack, an offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive in military language is an all-out attack or assault, so the definition works as a noun with 'is' joining.

clue.text: Willow often seen in elementary receptacles initially

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Willow is commonly found in basic baskets, as wicker.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a species of willow whose pliant shoots are used in basketry.

clue.text: On high inside rushed to get drunk

indicators.note: inside places the up word within the rushed word

parts.note: rushed means sped
on high means up

explanation.surface: Someone high up dashed off to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like being intoxicated but it is the past participle of drink; 'to get' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To sup is to drink in small mouthfuls, so its past participle matches drunk.

clue.text: Wasteful swine taking stick over nearly everything

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first part above the second
taking means the pig word takes in the stick word

parts.note: a swine is a pig
a rod is a stick

indicators.note: nearly means drop the final letter

parts.note: everything is all

explanation.surface: A wasteful pig takes a stick to almost everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The parable of the prodigal son, who ended up feeding swine, sits behind the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means recklessly extravagant, a synonym for wasteful.

clue.text: Yokels given fine, overlooking pounds and shillings

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving out, so the pounds letter is removed

parts.note: fine weather is pleasant
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
S is the abbreviation for shillings, the old British coin

explanation.surface: Country bumpkins are fined, with pounds and shillings in the reckoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Shillings were pre-decimal British coins worth a twentieth of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Peasants are rural labourers, and the word is used dismissively for unsophisticated country folk.

clue.text: Philander topless, somehow becoming extreme

indicators.note: somehow means the remaining letters are arranged in some other way
topless means the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A womaniser going topless becomes outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes P, leaving HILANDER, which 'somehow' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardline stance is uncompromising and extreme in its views.

clue.text: Atmosphere turned, perhaps around date for last judgement

indicators.note: turned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: an atmosphere is a mood

indicators.note: around means the say word goes round the date letter

parts.note: perhaps means say, as in for example

explanation.surface: The mood darkened around the date of reckoning.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian belief the final day of judgement for all souls is known as the day of doom.

clue.text: Relative's favourite's raised accordingly by name

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: a favourite is a pet; with the s it gives PETS
accordingly means so, therefore

explanation.surface: A family member's favourite is brought up accordingly by name.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a spouse's son from an earlier relationship, a relative by marriage.

clue.text: Feeble outcome, caught out by sweetheart

indicators.note: out means the caught letter is left out

parts.note: an outcome is an effect
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A weak result, with someone caught out by their lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes C from EFFECT; 'sweetheart' is read as the heart of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means weak and lacking vigour, a synonym for feeble.

clue.text: Fine and noble protecting independent American state

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: protecting means the noble word guards the other letter inside

parts.note: a lord is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A fine nobleman shields an independent figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Florida is the south-eastern state of the USA.

clue.text: Mature old burgundy's opening up in cellar

indicators.note: up in a down clue means all the pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: mature means aged

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of burgundy

explanation.surface: A mature old burgundy is opened in the wine cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine cellar or wine shop.

clue.text: Build up and knock down, they say

indicators.note: they say signals a word that sounds the same when spoken

parts.note: to raze a building is to knock it down

explanation.surface: Building up and knocking down sound the same, people claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a building is to construct it, to put it up.

clue.text: One covers smell of rot on dead bats

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Something masks the stench of decay on dead bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals but means mad, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A deodorant masks body odour, so it is something that covers a smell.

clue.text: Benefit of a fine screen for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means as heard by listeners

parts.note: a veil is a fine screen of fabric; with a it gives A VEIL

explanation.surface: A thin screen helps the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or benefit, as in to no avail.

clue.text: Arise as priest's last organised part of church

indicators.note: last means the final letter of the word priest

parts.note: to organise is to run, past tense ran
a spire is the tall pointed part of a church

explanation.surface: A priest's final arrangement concerns part of his church.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpire is to happen or come about, as a situation arises.

clue.text: Independence held back Ohio state

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: held means had, kept
O is an old abbreviation for Ohio

explanation.surface: Independence was withheld from the state of Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state in the north-western USA.

clue.text: Peels in a bra, accidentally showing bosom

indicators.note: accidentally means the letters fall into a new order by chance

explanation.surface: Someone peeling things in a bra accidentally reveals their chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bosom' looks like the chest but means close, as in bosom friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosom friends are very close, never apart, so the adjective means inseparable.
